I've read through the whole repo. Here's my mental model of it.

## What this is

`x3e unblocked games` — a **static, vanilla HTML/CSS/JS** games portal served from GitHub Pages at `https://gamebackup.github.io/`. No build step, no framework, no package manager: you edit files, push to `main`, and Pages deploys. [successor-guide.md](successor-guide.md) is the handover doc the original creator wrote; it's the single best orientation file in the repo.

This repo is only the **shell/storefront**. The actual games live in ~10 sibling repos under the `gamebackup` GitHub org (`standalone_games` … `_4`, `flash_games`, `emu_games`, `gba_games`, `pico8_games`, `itchio_games`, `fnf-mods`, plus single-game repos like `chord/`, `balz/`, `noomi/`). Each is a Pages project site mounted at `https://gamebackup.github.io/<repo>/<game>/`. Game buttons in `index.html` are just `onclick="playGame('<that url>')"`.

## File-by-file

- **[index.html](index.html)** (1,896 lines) — the whole app. Section order: `<head>` inline script (tab-cloak + theme pre-paint), game grid by genre via `playGame(url)`, then a series of `<script>` blocks at the bottom for search, particles, Halloween theme, mirror failover, volume, cloaking/settings UI, service-worker registration, the offline-preloader, update checker, countdown timer, and section collapse.
- **[style.css](style.css)** (1,468 lines) — dark theme, neon pink `#e61587`, glitch title, glass modals, 600px responsive.
- **[sw.js](sw.js)** (134 lines) — service worker. Cache name is `x3e-offline-v3`. `networkFirst` for `/emulatorjs/` (so updated emulator cores never pin stale), `cache-first` otherwise, and only for `gamebackup.github.io`. A `START_SESSION` message flips it to cache *any* origin for offline preloading. `CLEAR_GAME` is prefix-guarded to `https://gamebackup.github.io/`.
- **[finalproduct-v2.html](finalproduct-v2.html)** (25 lines) — the "give this to people" loader. Fetches the raw GitHub `index.html` and injects it, which is how it dodges filter blocks.
- **[404.html](404.html)**, **[dedications.html](dedications.html)** (unlinked floating page), **[read-the-button.html](read-the-button.html)** (a joke page).
- **[images/](images)** — served via jsdelivr (`cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/gamebackup/gamebackup.github.io@main/images/...`), not locally.

## Key mechanics

- **Version/update system:** `<meta name="x3e-version" content="2026/10/7-1">` at the top of `index.html`. The site polls the raw GitHub file every 10 min (Range bytes 0–1500) and shows a banner if it differs. `finalproduct-v2.html` depends on this tag too — **bumping it is mandatory on every notable change**.
- **Mirror failover:** `playGame` detects a `gamebackup.github.io/<repo>/` URL, then races the direct origin against six jsdelivr mirrors (direct gets a 2.5s budget, mirrors 7s). If a mirror wins, it injects a `<base>` tag and hands the game to the iframe as a blob URL. The last winner is remembered in `localStorage` (`x3e-mirror`).
- **Offline preloading:** settings → picker (max 5), hidden 1px iframes load each game while the SW runs a preload session, results tracked in `localStorage` (`x3e-cachedGames`). `NON_CACHEABLE_GAMES` excludes things like Hollow Knight, Celeste, PokeRogue, wikispeedruns, Gutenberg.
- **Tab cloaking** presets are duplicated **twice** (the head inline script and the main script) — the guide warns to update both.
- **Offline game overlay** is a `sandbox`ed iframe with a broad allowlist; scroll position is saved in `sessionStorage`.
- Star ratings in button text: `*` laggy, `**` probably playable, `***` won't run on Chromebooks.

## Things I noticed that are stale/broken

- **`manifest.json` is referenced** (`<link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.json">`) but **does not exist in the repo** — the PWA install from the changelog is silently broken.
- `index.html` loads CSS from the **absolute** `https://gamebackup.github.io/style.css`, not the local copy, so local edits to `style.css` don't show when testing `index.html` locally.
- The guide is out of date in places: it says `CACHE_NAME` is `x3e-offline-v2` (it's now `v3`), it doesn't know about the mirror-failover system, and the "~370 games" in §1 contradicts "272 games" in §12. Game count on the site is derived (`total buttons − 10`) and currently the header placeholder says 272.
- Recent history is mostly autogenerated `Update index.html` commits; the last few include a Halloween theme update, so `halloween` theme support and the pumpkin toggle are recent additions.

`worker.js` re-serves the x3e game files from a hostname you control, so the
games keep loading when `gamebackup.github.io` (or jsDelivr) is filtered.

It is a one-to-one pass-through:

```
https://<your-host>/standalone_games/2048/     ->  https://gamebackup.github.io/standalone_games/2048/
https://<your-host>/flash_games/games/btd1/    ->  https://gamebackup.github.io/flash_games/games/btd1/
```

So the games' relative *and* root-relative asset paths keep resolving, and no
HTML rewriting is needed. If the real origin is unreachable or missing a file,
the proxy falls back to jsDelivr. The upstream host is hard-coded, so this is
not an open proxy.

The same file runs on Cloudflare Workers, Deno Deploy and Vercel edge
functions, because they all accept a `fetch(request)` handler.

---

## Read this first: the hostname is the whole problem

The proxy only helps if **its own hostname is not categorized/blocked**. Shared
platform subdomains — `*.workers.dev`, `*.deno.dev`, `*.vercel.app`,
`*.netlify.app` — are used by thousands of sites doing exactly this, so filters
usually categorize them wholesale, and they can change under you because you
don't control them.

**A domain you own (~$10/year) pointed at any of these platforms is the only
durable answer.** Deploying to a platform default and hoping is a coin flip.
Test from the actual filtered network, not from home.

---

## Deploy

### Deno Deploy (no Cloudflare account needed)

1. Push this repo to GitHub.
2. In the [Deno Deploy](https://dash.deno.com) dashboard, create a project and
   connect the repo.
3. Set the entrypoint to `proxy/worker.js`. It auto-detects the default export.
4. Add your custom domain under the project's Domains settings.

Or from the CLI:

```sh
deployctl deploy --project=<your-project> proxy/worker.js
```

### Cloudflare Workers

```sh
npx wrangler deploy proxy/wrangler.toml
```

Then add a custom domain: Workers → your worker → Settings → Domains & Routes.
The `*.workers.dev` hostname is commonly filtered on its own.

### Vercel / Netlify

Both can run this, but they need a thin wrapper so the `fetch`-style handler is
detected. On Vercel, add `api/[[...path]].js`:

```js
export const config = { runtime: 'edge' };
export { default } from '../../proxy/worker.js';
```

On Netlify, put a wrapper in `netlify/edge-functions/proxy.js` and route it with
`export default (request, context) => handler(request, context);` plus a
`[[path]]` entry in `netlify.toml`.

## 1. Mirror failover hardened — [index.html](index.html)

- **More origins, and they're now per-host correct.** Added `cdn.statically.io`, `raw.githack.com` and `rawcdn.githack.com` alongside the six jsDelivr endpoints. Because these three use `/main/` where jsDelivr uses `@main/`, each entry is now `{ label, prefix(repo) }` instead of a shared string template — the old single-prefix loop could never have expressed them.
- **Falls back in parallel instead of one-at-a-time.** The old loop tried hosts strictly sequentially: on a filtered network the worst case was roughly 2.5s + 9 × 7s ≈ **65 seconds** before it gave up. Probes now start simultaneously (direct origin immediately, the rest staggered 300 ms apart) and the first host to answer wins via `Promise.any`, hard-capped at 12s. A blocked host costs milliseconds.
- **Dead hosts are remembered.** A host that fails is skipped for 6 hours, so you stop paying for known-bad origins on every launch. Critically, only *network* failures count — a 404 for one missing game no longer disables a good mirror for everything else (I caught and fixed this during review).
- **Fixed a pre-existing breakage:** games that are a single `.html` file rather than a directory (e.g. `standalone_games/hk/hollow knight.html`) used to get a slash appended, producing a nonsense `<file>.html/index.html` probe URL. Files and directories are now handled separately.

## 2. Proxy — [proxy/worker.js](proxy/worker.js)

A portable, ~120-line edge function: path-preserving pass-through (`/<repo>/<path>` → `gamebackup.github.io/<repo>/<path>`), jsDelivr fallback when the real origin fails, CORS headers, edge caching, and stripped `set-cookie`/`x-frame-options`/CSP. The upstream host is hard-coded, so it is **not** an open proxy. One file runs on Cloudflare Workers, Deno Deploy and Vercel edge, because it exports a function that also carries a `fetch` property.

Also added [proxy/README.md](proxy/README.md), [proxy/wrangler.toml](proxy/wrangler.toml), [proxy/package.json](proxy/package.json) and [proxy/smoke-test.mjs](proxy/smoke-test.mjs).

## 3. Wiring — [sw.js](sw.js)

`X3E_PROXY_ORIGIN` is a config constant in **both** [index.html](index.html) and [sw.js](sw.js); set both to your deployed origin (leave `''` to disable). +# x3e game proxy
+
+`worker.js` re-serves the x3e game files from a hostname you control, so the
+games keep loading when `gamebackup.github.io` (or jsDelivr) is filtered.
+
+It is a one-to-one pass-through:
+
+```
+https://<your-host>/standalone_games/2048/     ->  https://gamebackup.github.io/standalone_games/2048/
+https://<your-host>/flash_games/games/btd1/    ->  https://gamebackup.github.io/flash_games/games/btd1/
+```
+
+So the games' relative *and* root-relative asset paths keep resolving, and no
+HTML rewriting is needed. If the real origin is unreachable or missing a file,
+the proxy falls back to jsDelivr. The upstream host is hard-coded, so this is
+not an open proxy.
+
+The same file runs on Cloudflare Workers, Deno Deploy and Vercel edge
+functions, because they all accept a `fetch(request)` handler.
+
+---
+
+## Read this first: the hostname is the whole problem
+
+The proxy only helps if **its own hostname is not categorized/blocked**. Shared
+platform subdomains — `*.workers.dev`, `*.deno.dev`, `*.vercel.app`,
+`*.netlify.app` — are used by thousands of sites doing exactly this, so filters
+usually categorize them wholesale, and they can change under you because you
+don't control them.
+
+**A domain you own (~$10/year) pointed at any of these platforms is the only
+durable answer.** Deploying to a platform default and hoping is a coin flip.
+Test from the actual filtered network, not from home.
+
+---
+
+## Deploy
+
+### Deno Deploy (no Cloudflare account needed)
+
+1. Push this repo to GitHub.
+2. In the [Deno Deploy](https://dash.deno.com) dashboard, create a project and
+   connect the repo.
+3. Set the entrypoint to `proxy/worker.js`. It auto-detects the default export.
+4. Add your custom domain under the project's Domains settings.
+
+Or from the CLI:
+
+```sh
+deployctl deploy --project=<your-project> proxy/worker.js
+```
+
+### Cloudflare Workers
+
+```sh
+npx wrangler deploy proxy/wrangler.toml
+```
+
+Then add a custom domain: Workers → your worker → Settings → Domains & Routes.
+The `*.workers.dev` hostname is commonly filtered on its own.
+
+### Vercel / Netlify
+
+Both can run this, but they need a thin wrapper so the `fetch`-style handler is
+detected. On Vercel, add `api/[[...path]].js`:
+
+```js
+export const config = { runtime: 'edge' };
+export { default } from '../../proxy/worker.js';
+```
+
+On Netlify, put a wrapper in `netlify/edge-functions/proxy.js` and route it with
+`export default (request, context) => handler(request, context);` plus a
+`[[path]]` entry in `netlify.toml`.
+
+---
+
+## Verify it works
+
+Locally, against the real upstream (6 checks, including a simulated filter block
+to prove the jsDelivr fallback engages):
+
+```sh
+node proxy/smoke-test.mjs
+```
+
+After deploying, from the filtered network:
+
+```sh
+curl -i https://<your-host>/
+# -> "x3e game proxy is running."
+
+curl -sI https://<your-host>/standalone_games/2048/
+# -> HTTP/2 200, content-type: text/html
+```
+
+A 200 here from a *filtered* connection is the only result that means anything.
+
+---
+
+## Wire it into the site
+
+Set the same value in **two** places — clicking a game has to route through the
+proxy, and offline caching has to accept the proxied responses:
+
+1. `X3E_PROXY_ORIGIN` in **index.html** (in the `── Mirror failover ──` block).
+2. `X3E_PROXY_ORIGIN` in **sw.js** (at the top).
+
+Use just the origin, no trailing slash or path:
+
+```js
+const X3E_PROXY_ORIGIN = 'https://x3e.example.com';
+```
+
+Leave it as `''` to disable the proxy. The proxy is tried second, right after a
+quick probe of the real origin, and it is remembered as the winner once it
+serves a game — so a filtered origin only costs one short probe per session.
+
+`finalproduct-v2.html` does **not** need to change: it fetches `index.html` at
+runtime, so existing users pick the new config up automatically.
